title: Maryland, second-line songs and when the blues were played
summary: Maryland played like the Eureka, return songs for the second line, and blues kept for late dances and slow walking time in the street.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Maryland we're talking about. Oh. At least I was talking about Maryland.

Yeah, that's an old march Maryland. What about songs coming back in those days? What would you play coming back? For the second line? Oh like from a funeral? Mm-hmm. Well they played like the Sheik, Maury, put on your old gray bonnet. Yeah, those three numbers, I'd about hold them up. Old gray bonnet used to be a hit one time. When did the band start playing blues? Well those blues was mostly used in like dance halls. And when they'd get around about 10 o'clock, 11 o'clock, they'd start playing blues. They'd have a lot of jump numbers until around about that time. When they'd get late they'd play blues. When did they start playing blues in the street? Well if somebody would ask for a blues like that, those second lines, they'd get together and ask for a blues, they could play a blues in walk time. They'd play St. Louis blues and sometimes the old blues.
